messages.subject: Re: convert from feaure to meta-feature
messages.body_plain:
I'm afraid there is no way to correctly convert the feature level counts into meta-feature level. Adding counts to all the features belonging to the same meta-feature doesn't give you the correct meta-feature level counts since a read may be counted multiple times (if multi-assignment was allowed in feature-level counting) or wrongly discarded (if multi-assignment was disallowed in feature-level counting).

The proper way is to re-run featureCounts on the meta-feature mode.

messages.subject_clean: featurecounts contain multiple values in Chr, Start, End and Strand
messages.body_plain:
The 'Length' column gives the effective length of each gene, which is the total number of unique bases in exons that belong to the gene.

Regarding the output from meta-feature level counting, featureCounts has to output chr names for each exon because of the possibility that some genes are located on more than one chromosome. It is not hard to reduce these chr names to unique names:

> unlist(lapply(strsplit(c("Chr01;Chr01;Chr01;Chr01;Chr01", "Chr02;Chr02;Chr02"),';'),unique))
[1] "Chr01" "Chr02"

messages.subject: Re: featureCounts −−fracOverlapFeature and clipped reads
messages.body_plain:
Hi Malcolm,

The fracOverlapFeature option dictates the fraction in the feature that is overlapped by the read. A read can be longer than the feature but the feature has to have its full length covered by the read (or read-pair if "-p" is specified).

Please be aware that the overlapping requirement only works on "features" (eg exons) even if featureCounts runs on the meta-feature mode. Say, a gene has two exons, and a read only fully covers with one of the exons, then this read is still assigned to this gene when "fracOverlapFeature" is set to 1 and featureCounts runs on the meta-feature mode.

Cheers,
Yang

messages.subject: Re: featureCounts −−fracOverlapFeature and clipped reads
messages.body_plain:
"if a feature is overlapped only by the soft-trimmed end of a read", ie if the mapped part/parts in the read don't overlap with a feature, then this feature will not be considered when assigning this read to features/meta features.

Say, if a read has a CIGAR string of "50S50M" in the BAM file, and the "50S" part overlaps with an exon, but the "50M" part doesn't overlap with this exon, then this exon is not considered for assigning this read.
